clue.text: Expedient seamstress might

definitions.meaning: an expedient is a stopgap, a temporary way of getting by
a seamstress might run up a shift, the loose dress

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's power is said to be a matter of convenience.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into MAKE SHIFT: a shift is a simple dress or chemise, so making one is a seamstress's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a stopgap arrangement, and the phrase for running up a plain dress.

clue.text: Ready and marshalled, men-at-arms

indicators.note: marshalled means arranged in order, as troops are drawn up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the hyphens are ignored, leaving nine letters

explanation.surface: Soldiers stand prepared and lined up for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective about the troops; it is the surname of the hero of Captain Marryat's novel Masterman Ready, so the answer is the name that goes with it, and 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterman Ready is the title character of Marryat's 1841 children's novel, the old seaman whose first name partners Ready.

clue.text: Honour among thieves

parts.note: an honour in card games is a high court card, and the jack is also a word for a rogue, so the card counts among villains

explanation.surface: The proverb that even criminals keep faith with one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is a red herring: in bridge an honour is a top card, and the card in question also means a dishonest rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack is an honour card at bridge, and the word also means a scoundrel.

clue.text: Key note one found in airport

parts.note: so (soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: found in means the numeral sits inside the airport's name

parts.note: Luton is an airport north of London
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An important note, one picked up at a terminal building.
explanation.walkthrough: LUTON is an airport just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is the answer to a puzzle, such as the printed answers to a crossword.

clue.text: I printed letters wrongly in bold

indicators.note: the letters set wrongly signals that the two words' letters come out in a different order

explanation.surface: A typesetter confesses to a misprint in a bold typeface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bold' suggests heavy type, matching the printing story, but it means fearless; 'letters wrongly' rearranges IPRINTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrepid person is fearless and daring.

clue.text: Miss O'Ferrall's hat

definitions.meaning: ... O'Ferrall is the heroine of George du Maurier's novel of that name
a soft felt hat with a dented crown

explanation.surface: The headgear belonging to a young woman named O'Ferrall.
explanation.walkthrough: The hat took its name from the stage version of du Maurier's novel, whose heroine is Trilby O'Ferrall.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine's first name in du Maurier's novel, and the felt hat named after that book's stage production.

clue.text: Scholar to follow first principles

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree

explanation.surface: An academic is urged to stick to the basic tenets of the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a body of settled doctrine, the core tenets accepted as beyond question.

clue.text: Deny one's depressed about it

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: down means low in spirits
one is I, and the 's is is, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to admit they feel low about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', I plus IS... it gives I and S; 'it' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge, to repudiate.

clue.text: Go and get soil for his analysis

definitions.text: Go and get soil for his analysis

indicators.note: analysis means breaking something into parts, so the words are broken down and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to fetch earth samples so a scientist can test them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the fodder words and adds no letters; 'analysis' rearranges GOGETSOIL, and the whole clue also describes a rock scientist at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies rocks and earth would send for soil samples to test.

clue.text: Jack upended Miss West by the waist

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is one too

indicators.note: upended in a down clue means turned upside down, so the name reads bottom to top

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: A sailor turned the film star over, holding her round the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The waist of a ship is its middle section, so abeam, at right angles to the keel, is level with the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam means at right angles to a ship's length, opposite its middle section.

clue.text: Will Miss O'Hara get a hearing?

indicators.note: getting a hearing means the name is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Scarlett O'Hara is the heroine of Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: A question of whether Gone with the Wind's heroine will be allowed to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the verb opening a question, but it is the definition: Will Scarlet is one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws, whose surname is said like Miss O'Hara's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Will Scarlet is one of Robin Hood's Merry Men, so the name partners Will.

clue.text: Heroin's concealed, not far out at sea

indicators.note: concealed means disguised, the letters of the drug's name dressed up as something else

parts.note: the possessive's S counts here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A drug haul has been hidden close to the coast by smugglers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' here signals disguise: the seven letters HEROINS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore waters lie close to the coast, near the land rather than out in open sea.

clue.text: Chosen to give some of the lectures

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone has been selected to deliver part of a lecture series.
explanation.definitionFit: Elect as an adjective means picked out or selected, as in a president-elect.

clue.text: Space for Katisha to display her best feature?

definitions.text: Space for Katisha to display her best feature?

parts.words: Space for Katisha to display her best feature?
parts.note: Katisha in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado boasts of her left elbow, which people come miles to see, so she needs room to show that joint off

explanation.surface: A request for room so a Mikado character can show off her charms.
explanation.walkthrough: Katisha is the elderly lady in The Mikado who prides herself on her left elbow; the clue reads the phrase for room to move literally, as room for an elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means enough room to move freely, here taken literally as room for a prized joint.

clue.text: Tree acted in "Show Boat'

definitions.meaning: a flowering tree or shrub with large showy blooms
... Hawks is the heroine of the musical Show Boat, who becomes an actress on the riverboat

explanation.surface: Someone named Tree once had a part in the musical Show Boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree' reads like the actor Herbert Beerbohm Tree, a famous name on the stage, but it is just the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of flowering trees, and the name of the riverboat heroine of the Kern and Hammerstein musical.

clue.text: Fighter pleased round one is over

parts.note: glad means pleased
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: is over means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rota is a round of duties taken in turn

explanation.surface: A boxer is happy that the first round has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wants to be a boxing round; it is a rota, turned over to give ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a Roman arena combatant, a professional fighter.

clue.text: Member doesn't start to get up

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to climb is to get up a slope or ladder

explanation.surface: A club member fails to rise to their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the body is an arm or a leg.

clue.text: Ran through the sea, a certain Edward

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea
a certain person is one person
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward dashed through the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran through' looks like a past tense of running; it means stabbed with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone through is to pierce them with a blade fixed to a rifle.

clue.text: Encounter in which shells may be aimed at Mortlake

definitions.text: Encounter in which shells may be aimed at Mortlake

parts.words: Encounter in which shells may be aimed at Mortlake
parts.note: shells are light racing rowing boats, and Mortlake on the Thames is the finish of the annual Oxford and Cambridge contest

explanation.surface: An artillery battle with shells fired at a London riverside suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shells' suggests artillery; they are racing boats, and Mortlake is the finishing point of the Oxford v Cambridge race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual rowing contest between Oxford and Cambridge, raced from Putney up to Mortlake.

clue.text: Fill up again let it just trickle, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to restore a supply, top up once more
a battery can be given a slow trickle of current to restore it

explanation.surface: Topping up a tank by letting the liquid flow slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: A trickle charge is a slow, low current used to restore a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: replenishing a supply, and restoring a battery, perhaps with a slow trickle of current.

clue.text: Close up tight

definitions.meaning: tight with money, mean or stingy, an old sense of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to shut something firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: nearby, and the dated meaning of mean or miserly with money.

clue.text: For two points, have a go at woodwork

parts.note: E and S, two points of the compass, east and south
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: A carpentry lesson where each attempt earns a couple of points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woodwork' looks like carpentry; it is a playful definition for the work of managing woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestry is the management of woods and forests, so it is work with woods, quite literally.

clue.text: Stop sounding foreign

indicators.note: sounding means the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: Finnish is a foreign language, from Finland

explanation.surface: An instruction to quit talking in a foreign accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' stands for one example, Finnish, the language of Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is to stop, to bring something to an end.

clue.text: Manufacture cosmetics

explanation.surface: Producing beauty products.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to put together or fabricate, and face paint such as lipstick and powder.

clue.text: Pretended to be different, and so it is

indicators.note: different means the letters of the phrase appear in another order

explanation.surface: Someone claimed to be unusual, and indeed they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be different' runs together in the surface, but 'to be' is only a link and 'different' alone makes ANDSOITIS into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan so-disant means self-styled or so-called, describing a claim not borne out.

clue.text: Cornwall, for example, a peninsula to be overrun

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, SW
an arm of land is a narrow peninsula

explanation.surface: A Cornish headland about to be invaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the far south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm is to be crowded or teeming, as a place swarms with visitors.

clue.text: Don't keep unfinished port

indicators.note: unfinished means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: if you don't keep something you haven't got it

explanation.surface: Advice not to hold on to a half-built harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't keep' gives the contraction HAVEN'T; the apostrophe is ignored and 'unfinished' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a harbour or sheltered anchorage for ships.

clue.text: Serviceman using rocket transport

parts.note: the V1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War, written VI
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A soldier rides on a missile as his means of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceman' suggests the armed forces; here it is a clergyman who takes church services.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest who conducts church services.

clue.text: Position of cavalryman with a foot in either camp

definitions.meaning: a rider sits with one leg each side of the horse

definitions.text: with a foot in either camp

explanation.surface: A horseman who refuses to commit to either side of a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: sitting legs apart over a horse, and figuratively straddling two sides of an argument.

clue.text: A date — October, perhaps when fruit appears

annotationWithheld.why: A date - October, perhaps - when fruit appears (7): printed so on the scan, but no parse gives APRICOT; neither 'A date' nor 'October, perhaps' supplies its letters and a search found no explanation
annotationWithheld.clue: A date — October, perhaps when fruit appears

clue.text: Several days' walk

definitions.meaning: a month is a run of several days, thirty-one of them for this one
to walk in step, as soldiers do

explanation.surface: A trek lasting a few days.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the third month of the year, and to walk in a military way.

clue.text: Quiet judge made a mistake — promoted

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
a ref, short for referee, judges a game
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken referee blundered, yet still won advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be preferred is an old way of saying advanced to a higher post or office.
